case.case_title: Chandra Kalyanie Perera and Another v. Captain Siriwardena and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1992] 1 Sri L.R. 251

clause.text: No person shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the treatment of the 1st petitioner during detention constituted torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment in violation of Article 11 of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The 1st petitioner alleged she was manacled, beaten with a hose, hung by her manacles, beaten until she confessed, and subjected to sexual harassment by the 1st respondent during detention.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied the allegations of torture and inhuman treatment, asserting that the 1st petitioner was subjected only to severe interrogation and rough treatment which did not amount to a violation of Article 11.
key_facts: The 1st petitioner was detained under Emergency Regulations and subjected to interrogation and confrontation.
She alleged physical abuse including being manacled, beaten, hung by manacles, and sexual harassment by the 1st respondent.
The 1st respondent left the army and the country before the hearing.
Affidavits supporting the allegations were either retracted or considered unreliable.
The court found the evidence did not establish grave inhuman treatment amounting to a violation of Article 11.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 11 prohibits torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. The court examined whether the treatment endured by the petitioner met this threshold.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court accepted that the petitioner was subjected to severe interrogation and rough treatment but found the evidence insufficient to prove treatment of the gravity required to constitute a violation of Article 11.
principles_established: Severe interrogation and rough treatment do not necessarily amount to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment under Article 11.
The burden of proof lies on the petitioner to establish grave inhuman treatment.
precedents_cited: Mrs. W. M. K. de Silva v. Chairman, Ceylon Fertilizer Corporation

outcome.holding: The court held that the alleged infringement of Article 11 was not established and dismissed that claim.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: The petitioner claimed violations of Article 11 due to alleged torture and inhuman treatment during detention. The court's reasoning and ultimate dismissal of this claim directly involved interpretation and application of Article 11.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The 1st petitioner was subjected to severe interrogation and rough treatment but the evidence did not establish grave inhuman treatment constituting a violation of Article 11.
